text:
nina: RFC follow-up: proposing a 'splice-and-prune' migration for the enrichment/runtime surface. Key idea: instead of a big-bang extract, we splice in a tiny compatibility layer that can forward, mirror, and normalize. plan focuses on progressive ownership transfer + tech-debt paydown windows.

omar: high-level +1. can you list failure modes and safety nets?

nina: sure: 1) semantic divergence (detected via semantic checks), 2) cache incompatibility (kv key shape), 3) perf regression, 4) partial-deploy mismatch. safety nets: sampled mirroring, per-tenant token-bucket caps, response-scoring alarms, and feature-flagged compatibility modes.

celine: about the token-bucket caps  what's the ramp cadence? doubling is scary for big tenants.

nina: propose: start 0.25% of tenant qps, linear add +0.25% every 20m up to 5%, then multiply by 1.2 every hour after confidence window. will be adjustable per-tenant.

patrick: ops checklist request: include a scheduled "debt-prune" window where we remove the splice once tenant is stable. ops needs signals to batch prunes.

nina: lifecycle policy: mark tenant stable after 10 days with <0.05% semantic diffs and <0.2% error delta; enqueue for prune during weekly low-traffic window. prunes are reversible for 72h.

omar: parity detection  hashes are noisy for streaming responses. add semantic metrics: intent-stability (categorical match), slot-F1, and token-level overlap for deterministic outputs.

nina: will add those. monitoring tiers: tier-0 quick signals (hash, p95), tier-1 semantic evals for flagged prompts, tier-2 nightly deterministic run on canonical prompt set.

patrick: can we attach a migration-id to every request so we can slice traces and logs?

nina: yes  X-Migration-Id and X-Migration-Owner headers, plus tracing tag migration.id. include in log backfill queries.

migrate-bot: Created MIG-777: "splice-and-prune: feature-flag + per-tenant ramp infra spike". Assignee: infra. ETA: 3d. Link: https://tracker/redwood/MIG-777

celine: test matrix please: kv skew scenarios, hot-path auth cache misses, load-surge with mixed prompt lengths, streaming cutovers, rollback under 10% and 50% traffic.

nina: drafting test matrix. we'll include fault injection to simulate partial dependency failure and ensure graceful fallback to legacy path.

omar: observability ask: dash tiles for percent routed to splice, per-tenant ramp curve, semantic-diff histogram by tenant, migration-id filter, and a rolling 24h auto-prune candidate list.

nina: noted. also adding a "debt-paydown" column for each tenant: estimated code paths removed once splice pruned. helpful for PM prioritization.

patrick: security note: ensure splice normalizes auth headers and doesn't widen token audience. security review required before canary.

nina: will request security review in RFC addendum.

celine: small UX nicety: add a "dry-run" mode where splice receives mirrored traffic but never influences routing, with diffs recorded. helps measure risk without user impact.

nina: included: mirror-only mode + mirror-sample rate param.

migrate-bot: MIG-777 updated: dry-run included, added infra spike card.

omar: timeline suggestion: infra spike this week, small tenant canary next week, progressive ramp over 3 weeks per cohort, prune waves scheduled monthly.

nina: will put timeline in addendum. drafting rollout snippet (yaml-like): 
```
rollout:
  name: "splice-and-prune"
  phases:
    - phase: dry_run
      mirror_rate: 0.05
      duration_days: 3
    - phase: canary
      per_tenant_ramp: { start_fraction: 0.0025, linear_step: 0.0025, step_mins: 20, max_fraction: 0.05 }
    - phase: cohort_ramp
      cohort_multiplier: 1.2
      confidence_window_hours: 24
  monitors: ["semantic-diff", "latency-p95", "error-rate"]
  prune_policy: { stable_days: 10, max_semantic_diff: 0.0005 }
```

patrick: looks good. once addendum posted I'll coordinate ops windows and prune automation.

nina: thanks all. I'll post RFC addendum today with dash mocks, test matrix, perf targets, rollback playbook, and a tech-debt accounting table mapping splice removal to code simplifications.
